identity.name: Sodium stearoyl-2-lactylate
synonyms: Sodium salts of stearoyl lactylic acids

function.mechanism: Interacts at fat-water and dough interfaces, improving emulsion stability and dough handling/structure in bakery systems.

adi.basis: Group ADI for E481 and E482, expressed as lactic acid (EFSA re-evaluation).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation concluded no safety concern for reported uses/use levels; no genotoxicity concern identified in the opinion summary.

fda.notes: Regulated as a direct food additive with category-specific maximum use levels; no dedicated Part 184 GRAS listing for sodium stearoyl lactylate was identified in current eCFR part text.

adi.basis: ADI listed in WHO JECFA record for sodium stearoyl-2-lactylate.

concerns.summary: An in vitro fecal microbiota study reported that 0.025% SSL reduced butyrate-producing taxa, reduced butyrate, and increased LPS/flagellin-associated pro-inflammatory potential.
A published case report described allergic contact dermatitis linked to sodium stearoyl lactylate exposure.
Belgian dietary exposure modeling found potential ADI exceedance in children under conservative assumptions; exceedance persisted in a small subset under refined assumptions.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA re-evaluation (2013) set a group ADI and did not find a safety concern for reported use levels.
A 1-year rat oral study reported no toxicologically significant adverse effects at tested doses and identified a high NOAEL.
JECFA and FDA continue to permit use under defined conditions and limits.

populations: children with high intake of bakery products
high consumers under conservative maximum-use assumptions
adi_exceedance.notes: Belgian data showed substantial potential exceedance under MPL-based Tier 2 estimates, but much lower exceedance under measured-concentration Tier 3 estimates (small residual child exceedance).

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory consensus supports safety at authorized uses with established ADIs and explicit use limits, while in vitro microbiome signals and child-exposure edge cases justify caution but not escalation to moderate/high risk.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI 22 mg/kg bw/day (E481+E482) with no safety concern at reported uses
FDA approval under 21 CFR 172.846 with explicit concentration limits
In vitro microbiome perturbation signal without direct clinical confirmation
Child intake exceedance possible in some exposure scenarios
